title: Drama: Classes of fire
body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: THE WRONG BUCKET
SUBJECT / TOPIC: INTEGRATED SCIENCE / Classes of fire
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
AGE RATING: 10+ (student-safe)
DURATION: 8 minutes
VISUAL STYLE: naturalistic live-action look with clear prop inserts (or 2D/3D cartoon adaptation of the same blocking)

LEARNING TIE-IN: Stop a small Class B fuel spill fire without making it worse

LOGLINE: A market stall fire nearly worsens when someone reaches for water until the fire triangle and class rules redirect the response.

WORLD & CAST

• Setting / era: EXT. open-air market stall, afternoon
• OWINO: stall helper, brave but untrained. Costume: cap, apron.
• SERGEANT ACHIENG: nearby safety marshal. Costume: high-vis vest.
• TRADER MUTHONI: stall owner. Costume: lesso, sturdy shoes.

SCREENPLAY

SCENE 1 — EXT./INT. OPENING LOCATION — DAY

ACTION: OWINO enters the world of the story with a clear goal: Stop a small Class B fuel spill fire without making it worse. Camera follows hands and faces, not a chalkboard.

OWINO
If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Wide establishing → medium two-shot. Ambient authentic location SFX. Soft hopeful underscore.

SCENE 2 — SAME / NEARBY — DAY

ACTION: Obstacle appears. Stakes rise. Props related to the science idea are handled as real objects, not lecture aids.

OWINO
It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

TRADER MUTHONI
If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Close-ups on props and worried eyes. Tension riser.

OWINO
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 3 — CONFRONTATION — DAY

ACTION: WRONG WAY: Owino throws water on burning oil/petrol-soaked rags. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action and argument — characters never read notes aloud.

OWINO
See? I did what everyone does.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Handheld urgency. Cut to the failed result.

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY/NIGHT

ACTION: A clue appears through action — a label, a measurement, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken as dialogue while doing.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.

OWINO
Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Insert shots of evidence. Music shifts from tension to curiosity.

OWINO
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 5 — SECOND ATTEMPT — DAY

ACTION: RIGHT WAY: They cut fuel/oxygen appropriately and evacuate, matching fire class. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.

OWINO
This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

TRADER MUTHONI
I can see the difference already.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Cleaner framed shots; success micro-beats.

SCENE 6 — COMPLICATION — DAY

ACTION: A new obstacle or time pressure forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.

TRADER MUTHONI
We are not done. Another problem just arrived.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Parallel cut or ticking clock motif without graphic peril.

OWINO
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY

ACTION: Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result; still no voice-over lecture.

OWINO
It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Warm wider shot; relieved faces; result hero insert.

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY

ACTION: Final acted beat tying emotion to the learning without reading notes aloud.

TRADER MUTHONI
Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.

OWINO
And we will check the evidence first.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Slow push-in; music resolves.

OWINO
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

SERGEANT ACHIENG
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

BOOKENDS

• COLD OPEN (max 10s): Quick hook image of the failed first attempt — then cut to title THE WRONG BUCKET.
• CLOSING REFLECTION CARD (max 10s): On-screen question — Why is water unsuitable for some fire classes? Answer must match lesson solutions (Petrol/electrical fires can worsen with water).

CAPTIONS

OWINO: If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.
SERGEANT ACHIENG: Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.
OWINO: It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.
TRADER MUTHONI: If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.
OWINO: See? I did what everyone does.
SERGEANT ACHIENG: And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.
SERGEANT ACHIENG: Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.
OWINO: Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.
OWINO: This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.
TRADER MUTHONI: I can see the difference already.
TRADER MUTHONI: We are not done. Another problem just arrived.
SERGEANT ACHIENG: Same science. Fresh situation. Go.
OWINO: It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.
SERGEANT ACHIENG: Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.
TRADER MUTHONI: Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.
OWINO: And we will check the evidence first.

ASSET LIST

• Characters: OWINO, SERGEANT ACHIENG, TRADER MUTHONI
• Costumes: as listed above
• Locations: EXT. open-air market stall, afternoon
• Props: topic-authentic objects for Classes of fire
• Key shots: failed attempt insert, evidence insert, successful payoff insert

Study pages available for fidelity: 20
DRAMA NOTE: No voice-over of lesson notes. Meaning travels through action and in-character dialogue.

sources.excerpt: -Classes of Fire. Fires can be classified between four and seven classes. The following are six classes of fire mostly widely used and accepted.
